correctness.rationale: The complete vertex set is reconstructed from the half-integral odd-cycle-support criterion: on K_n, only 0, unit vectors, and half-support indicators of cardinality at least three occur. By uniqueness and S_n symmetry any smallest-sphere center is t times the all-ones vector. Exact distance formulas by support cardinality prove that only e_i and potentially the all-half vector can support the ball, and that the simplex barycenter ball is feasible precisely through dimension six. At dimension seven the all-half distance forces a new center obtained by equating two squared distances. Every formula is valid for the entire claimed integer range; explicit positive contact barycentric coefficients provide a global minimax and uniqueness certificate, with strict distance separation for all noncontacts. The squared-gap algebra and asymptotic are exact.

originality.rationale: The primary 2017 circuit-diameter paper was inspected in the complete fractional-stable-set section and its surrounding main results; it contains no Euclidean minimum enclosing sphere, circumradius, or contact theorem. The earlier Hamano--Hibi--Ohsugi vertex-description paper was inspected at the definition, Lemma 2.2, and its Ehrhart analysis and likewise does not determine the minimum sphere. Independent published-result, semantic-database, and indexed searches covered complete-graph, clique, all-half, Chebyshev-center, smallest enclosing ball, circumradius, seven-dimensional, and integer-relaxation-gap aliases. A cycle-graph fractional stable-set body agrees with the clique family at the triangle only; cycle-specific polytope geometry does not determine complete-graph contacts in higher dimensions.
residual_risks: The nonnegative pairwise-truncated orthant is a classical polytope; an old smallest-sphere formula could exist without the name fractional stable-set polytope.
An unpublished or differently indexed general theorem for convex hulls of half-indicator vectors could subsume the calculation.
The exact algebra is elementary once the vertex orbits are recognized, so independent rediscovery is plausible.
Search nonappearance is not a global novelty certificate.

value.rationale: The fractional stable-set polytope is the canonical linear-programming edge relaxation of the stable-set polytope, and the clique is the cleanest graph where integrality constraints collapse to a simplex. The exact Euclidean relaxation gap and its dimension-seven onset are mathematically motivated measures of how fractional vertices change the worst-case Euclidean geometry. The complete contact classification identifies the mechanism and the gap grows unbounded in radius (order sqrt(n) vs bounded for the integral stable-set simplex), so the result is a family-wide structural threshold rather than an arbitrary numerical exercise. It complements existing circuit-diameter and Ehrhart research without claiming results in those topics.
